items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: There was a man by my house two or three days ago by the name of Arthur [Aarons].

ctx.x: Beautiful. That man, you know what he used to do, Stan? Like, he'd see me sitting across the street from the hotel, on a stoop, old concrete stoop, legs stretched out on the sidewalk. You know, Lips would make it a point to come by and sit and talk with me and give me advice, and tell me the things to do, and he was just so jovial, and I'd listen. Oh, he and I would have the greatest conversations. He did that for most all bands. Come by and sit and

talk with them, on the street, on the sidewalk, on the curb, didn't make no difference. He was a beautiful man. There was a man by my house two or three days ago by the name of Arthur [Aarons]. He married Hot Lips' former wife, Elizabeth. And she passed here not too long ago, during last summer, somewhere around in there. And she told him, told her husband, who was Arthur [Hines], everything that she wanted done to her body. She said, I know I'm going to die and it's going to be soon. She had cancer of the…

So he did. She told him, say, you got to promise me, said, because I know I'm going to die. I don't want my body laying in the casket, in the ground, termites chewing me up and all that. I want to be cremated. So he did it. And so, here come this sister, the girl Elizabeth's sister -- I'm talking about Hot Lips' Page ex-wife. They were together, and so Elizabeth's sister came up and got on Arthur Hines to cremate her body, having it burn up into ashes. I mean, he caught the devil from her. Elizabeth's sister.
